title: How to check system requirements in Zoom on Mac: zoom system requirements mac in 2026
metaTitle: Zoom System Requirements Mac: How to Check on Your Mac
description: Zoom system requirements Mac: check your macOS version, Zoom Workplace build, memory and permissions. Steps use System Settings and the current app.
secondaryKeywords: Zoom camera and microphone permission Mac
intro: To check Zoom system requirements on a Mac, confirm your macOS version first, then your Zoom Workplace build, then the permissions Zoom needs. Zoom lists macOS 10.15 or later, a dual-core 2 GHz processor and 4 GB of RAM as the minimums, though one of its articles also says 10.14.
tldr: The minimum macOS for Zoom Workplace is 10.15 in Zoom's system requirements article. A separate permissions article says 10.14, so plan for 10.15.
Zoom lists a dual-core 2 GHz processor and 4 GB of RAM as minimums. It recommends a quad-core 2.5 GHz processor and 16 GB of RAM.
Check your version in Settings, then compare it with Zoom's release notes table. The newest macOS build listed there is 7.2.5 (build 90525).
Camera, Microphone, Screen and System Audio Recording, Files and Folders and Accessibility live in System Settings under Privacy & Security.

blocks.text: Three checks answer most questions about Zoom and your Mac. Check your macOS version, check your Zoom Workplace build, then check the permissions Zoom needs. The order matters. A permission switch does nothing on a Mac that is too old, and an old build can block sign-in before you reach a camera test. Work through the checks in order and you will see quickly whether the problem is your Mac, the app or a setting.
What Zoom requires on a Mac

Zoom's system requirements article covers Windows, macOS and Linux on one page. For macOS, it gives the minimum as macOS 10.15 or later. The processor minimum is a dual-core 2 GHz chip, and Zoom recommends a quad-core 2.5 GHz chip. Memory starts at 4 GB, with 16 GB recommended. The same article says Zoom Workplace 6.7.7 was the last version available for macOS releases below 10.15.

blocks.caption: Minimums and recommendations from Zoom's macOS requirements article

blocks.text: The 10.14 versus 10.15 conflict

Zoom's permissions article says the desktop app requires macOS 10.14 Mojave or higher. That disagrees with the 10.15 figure in the system requirements article. Treat 10.15 as the safe number. If your Mac runs 10.14, check Zoom's live pages before you trust either number.

blocks.title: Two Zoom articles, two numbers
blocks.text: Zoom's pages disagree on the minimum macOS version. Re-check both articles if your Mac is close to the line, and plan for the stricter figure until Zoom resolves it.
Check your macOS version and memory

Start with About This Mac, which you open from the Apple menu. The window shows your macOS version, your memory, and your chip or processor. Any macOS release at 10.15 or later meets Zoom's stated minimum. Memory is the figure people overlook. Zoom's floor is 4 GB, and it recommends 16 GB. Write down both numbers before you move on, because the permission checks say nothing about hardware.
Find the Zoom Workplace version

The desktop app used to be called Zoom. Zoom renamed it Zoom Workplace in version 6.0, in April 2024. If you see either name, you are in the same app. Zoom's help article for the desktop app says you open Settings by clicking your profile picture and choosing Settings. On version 6.7.0 and higher, the gear icon in the navigation bar also opens Settings.

Zoom's help article does not say where the version number appears on a Mac for version 7.x. Older guides send you to zoom.us > About Zoom, but I could not confirm that path for current builds. If you cannot find a number in Settings, use the update check instead. The update check works without it.
Compare your build with the latest release

Zoom's release notes table lists 7.2.5 (build 90525) as the newest macOS build, dated October 31, 2026. The table also lists 7.2.2 (build 88465) and 7.1.9 (build 88375) from September 24, 2026, and 7.2.1 (build 88329) from September 21, 2026. A build below the newest one is not automatically broken. It is still the first thing to fix when Zoom asks for an update.

Third-party download sites disagreed about the latest number while I checked. Some showed 7.2.2 and others showed 7.2.5. Use Zoom's table as the reference, and check it again before you rely on it, because the newest build changes.
The permissions Zoom asks for on a Mac

macOS asks for your approval before any app uses the camera, the microphone or other protected features. Zoom's permissions article lists the set the desktop app needs. Administrator access is required to change them. The list is short, but each item affects a different part of a meeting.

items: Camera: lets Zoom send your video in a meeting.
Microphone: lets Zoom send your voice.
Screen and System Audio Recording: needed for screen sharing and shared computer sound.
Files and Folders: listed as a required permission in Zoom's permissions article.
Accessibility: needed for remote control, according to Zoom's permissions article.

blocks.text: Zoom Rooms is a different case. Zoom's article says it needs only Camera and Microphone. If you run Zoom Rooms on a Mac, you can skip the screen and folder switches. Everyone else on the desktop app should check all five items on the list.
Zoom Web App uses browser permissions

The Zoom Web App runs in your browser, so it does not use the desktop list. You approve the browser instead. Zoom's web app article says to open System Settings, click Privacy & Security, then click Microphone, Camera or Screen & System Audio Recording. Tick the box beside your browser. The article names Google Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge. Microphone access is required on macOS Mojave (10.14) or later.
Minimum client versions and forced updates

Zoom sets a minimum client version every quarter, on the first weekend of February, May, August and November. For macOS, Zoom lists 6.0.2 as the minimum for enforcement on November 7, 2026, and again on February 6, 2027. The May 1, 2027 date is still to be determined. A build below the minimum can show Update Required and refuse to sign you in.

blocks.title: Timing an update
blocks.text: Update Zoom the day before an important meeting, not on the way into it. An update that runs just before a call eats the time you wanted for a test.
Errors that point to requirements or install problems

Three error messages cover most install and sign-in problems on a Mac. Update Required means your build is too old to sign in. Error code 10004 means the desktop client fails to auto-update. Error 10008 points to an install problem, and Zoom recommends checking the minimum requirements and freeing up storage. Each one has its own fix in the troubleshooting list.
A worked example: a Mac on macOS 10.14

Say your Mac runs macOS 10.14 Mojave, and Zoom will not sign you in. You open About This Mac and confirm the version. Then you read the two Zoom articles. One says 10.14 is enough, and the other gives 10.15 as the minimum. Plan for 10.15, because it is the stricter number and the one the system requirements article gives.

Zoom's notes say Zoom Workplace 6.7.7 was the last version for macOS below 10.15. So a Mac on 10.14 is limited to that build. Open Settings, note the version, and compare it with the release table. If Zoom says 10.15 is required, the Mac needs an OS upgrade or an older build, and that decision belongs to you or your IT team.
Mistakes people make when checking requirements

items: Checking the Web App and assuming the desktop app matches. Each has its own permissions and version.
Following an old guide that says zoom.us > About Zoom. Older guides may not match the current app, so check current steps first.
Turning a switch on and not restarting Zoom. When Zoom is open, the app prompts you to restart.
Missing the browser checkbox for the Web App. The Microphone or Camera category alone is not enough.
Trusting a version number from a download site. Those sites disagreed about the newest build.
Assuming 10.14 is enough. Zoom's two articles disagree, so check the live page.
Forgetting admin rights. Permission changes need an administrator account.

blocks.text: Apple silicon, Intel and managed Macs

A common question is whether Zoom has separate requirements for Apple silicon and Intel Macs. The sources I checked do not answer it. Zoom's requirements article does not address chip type, and neither does the download page. Do not assume the answer either way. If an install fails on one chip type, contact Zoom support with your exact macOS version and build number.

If your Mac belongs to a company or school, IT may control some of these steps. Zoom says that on macOS it uses WebView2 and Chromium Embedded Framework for some features. It downloads them automatically if they are missing, and admins should allowlist them on managed devices. Ask IT before you change anything on a managed Mac.
Numbers worth knowing

These figures come from Zoom's own articles and release table. The 10.15 and 4 GB numbers are the minimums Zoom lists. The 16 GB and quad-core figures are recommendations. The 7.2.5 build is the newest in the table at the time of writing, so check the table again before you rely on it.
What to do next

If your Mac passes every check and Zoom still misbehaves, the symptom points to the next step. A blank camera often comes down to permissions, so start with [how to grant camera access in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/grant-camera-access-in-zoom). Update trouble has its own guide: [how to update Zoom on Mac](/how-to/update-zoom-in-zoom). A stuck install is covered in [how to reinstall Zoom on Mac](/how-to/reinstall-zoom-in-zoom). A black screen during sharing is in [how to fix a black screen share in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/fix-a-black-screen-share-in-zoom).

faq.question: What is the minimum macOS version for Zoom on a Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom's system requirements article says macOS 10.15 or later. Its permissions article says macOS 10.14 Mojave or higher. Plan for 10.15, and check Zoom's live pages if your Mac runs 10.14.

faq.question: Is Zoom Workplace the same app as Zoom?
faq.answer: Yes. Zoom renamed the desktop app Zoom Workplace in version 6.0, in April 2024. Older guides still say Zoom, and the core steps in this guide still apply.

faq.question: How much memory does Zoom need on a Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom lists 4 GB of RAM as the minimum and 16 GB as recommended. A Mac at the 4 GB floor meets the minimum, but 16 GB is what Zoom recommends for the smoothest use.

faq.question: Does Zoom have separate requirements for Apple silicon and Intel Macs?
faq.answer: The sources I checked do not say. Zoom's requirements and download pages do not list chip-specific notes, so do not assume either way without a fresh check.

faq.question: Why does Zoom say Update Required?
faq.answer: Zoom sets a minimum client version every quarter. A build below that minimum cannot sign in. Click Update, or download the latest version from the Zoom Downloads page and install it with admin rights.

faq.question: Do I need admin rights to change Zoom permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. Zoom's macOS permissions article says administrator access is required. If your Mac is managed by work or school, ask your IT team to make the change.

faq.question: What if I cannot find the version number in Settings?
faq.answer: Zoom's help article does not say where the version appears on a Mac for 7.x builds. Use the update check instead, then compare with the release table, which lists 7.2.5 as the newest build.

faq.question: Will reinstalling Zoom fix a requirements error?
faq.answer: Sometimes. For error 10008, Zoom recommends reinstalling, checking that the Mac meets the minimum requirements, and freeing up storage. Antivirus software can also interfere, so check it too.

task: Check whether your Mac meets Zoom's requirements
appliesTo: Zoom Workplace desktop app and Zoom Web App on macOS 10.15 or later
requirements: An administrator account on the Mac, for permission changes
Internet access to check for and install Zoom updates
Zoom Workplace installed, or the Zoom Web App open in a supported browser

steps.name: Open About This Mac
steps.text: Click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of the screen, then choose About This Mac. Read the macOS version in the window. Any version at 10.15 or later meets Zoom's stated minimum. The same window shows your chip or processor and your memory.
steps.tip: Keep this window in mind. You need the memory figure for the hardware check.

steps.name: Open Zoom Workplace
steps.text: Open Zoom from Applications, Launchpad or the Dock. The desktop app is now called Zoom Workplace, so look for that name if you see it. The interface steps below match version 6.7.0 and later.
steps.tip: If you have an older build, the menu layout may differ slightly from the steps here.

steps.name: Open Settings from your profile
steps.text: Click your profile picture in the upper-right corner of the Zoom window, then choose Settings. On version 6.7.0 and higher, the gear icon in the navigation bar also opens Settings.
steps.tip: Settings has a Search bar. Use it to find the Camera or Microphone options quickly.

steps.name: Find the version number
steps.text: Look through Settings for the Zoom version. Zoom's help article does not show where the version appears on a Mac, so if you cannot find it, skip to step 5. Write down the number you see.
steps.tip: Do not trust version numbers from third-party download sites. Use Zoom's own release notes table.

steps.name: Check for updates
steps.text: Click your picture or initials in the upper-right corner and select Check for updates. Follow the prompts until Zoom reports that it is current or finishes installing.
steps.tip: If an update fails, look at the error code in the troubleshooting list below.

steps.name: Compare with the latest release
steps.text: Open Zoom's release notes table. The newest macOS build listed is 7.2.5 (build 90525), dated October 31, 2026. If your version is lower, the update in step 5 is the fix.
steps.tip: Use Zoom's table, not download sites. Third-party sites disagreed about the latest number.

steps.name: Open the Camera permission
steps.text: Click the Apple logo, then choose System Settings. Click Privacy & Security, then click Privacy. Under Privacy, click Camera. Repeat the same route for Microphone and Screen & System Audio Recording.
steps.tip: You need administrator access to change these switches.

steps.name: Turn on the Zoom switches
steps.text: Find Zoom in each list and turn its switch on. Do the same under Microphone and Screen & System Audio Recording. Also check Files and Folders. Turn on Accessibility only if you need remote control.
steps.tip: If Zoom is not listed, open it once so it can request the permission, then check again.

steps.name: Restart Zoom after a change
steps.text: If Zoom is open when you change a permission, the app prompts you to restart. Accept the prompt, or quit Zoom and open it again. The change takes effect after that restart.
steps.tip: A permission switch that looks correct can still fail until you restart Zoom.

steps.name: Check permissions for the Web App
steps.text: If you join in a browser, open Microphone, Camera or Screen & System Audio Recording in the same Privacy & Security area. Tick the checkbox next to your browser: Google Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge.
steps.tip: Zoom's article does not say whether to restart the browser. Try a restart if the permission still fails.

steps.name: Handle the Update Required message
steps.text: If Zoom shows Update Required, click Update. If the update fails, download the latest version from the Zoom Downloads page and install it with admin rights. You can also click Join from browser to join right away.
steps.tip: Note the version number in the message. It is the minimum build that will sign in.

troubleshooting.problem: Zoom says Update Required and will not sign me in
troubleshooting.fix: Click Update. If it fails, download the latest version from the Zoom Downloads page, install it with admin rights, then sign in again. Join from browser works as a short-term way into a meeting.

Click zoom.us in the menu bar, choose Uninstall Zoom, restart, then reinstall from zoom.us/download. If reinstall fails, allow Installer under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access and Files and Folders.

troubleshooting.problem: Error 10008 during an update or install
troubleshooting.fix: Reinstall Zoom, check that the Mac meets the minimum requirements, and free up storage. Antivirus software and other apps can interfere, so check whether they block the install.

troubleshooting.problem: Camera or microphone works in other apps but not in Zoom
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, check the Camera and Microphone switches for Zoom, then quit and reopen Zoom. The permission only applies after the restart.

troubleshooting.problem: Permission is on, but Zoom still cannot use it
troubleshooting.fix: Quit Zoom fully and reopen it. If Zoom was open when you made the change, the app asks you to restart for the change to take effect.

troubleshooting.problem: The Zoom Web App cannot use the microphone
troubleshooting.fix: Tick the checkbox next to your browser under Microphone in Privacy & Security. The article does not say whether a browser restart is needed, so try one if the problem remains.
